Welcome
'Plant, Nurture, Flourish, Serve'
A very warm welcome to our school website. We hope that you enjoy looking through all the different pages and getting a little flavour of our wonderful school.
Everything we do in school is encapsulated by our school vision: 'Plant, Nurture, Flourish, Serve' and this is something that all our children and staff members work so hard to cultivate every day. This is also encapsulated in our day-to-day work with parents/carers and the wider community, where we work in very close partnership to enable all our children to do the very best that they can, considering our twelve school values.
To look around our lovely school, please contact the school office and I will be delighted to show you around. As headteacher, I am always available for a conversation, and we pride ourselves on our 'open door' policy of working with parents and carers. I am very proud and feel privileged to be headteacher of Box and we would be delighted if you joined us here.
For more information about our school and to look around it, please feel feel to contact the school office to speak to me.
admin@box.wilts.sch.uk

History
Box School dates back to 1707 when Dame Rachel Speke left a bequest to the parish for ‘teaching poor children to read and instructing them in the knowledge and practice of the Christian religion, as professed and taught in the Church of England’. In April 2024, we became part of the Mosaic Partnership Trust.

pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Our vision is something that motivates and inspires us and keeps us focused on where we want to go as a school. It’s a vision for everyone in the school, the children, staff, parents and governors. Our vision is:
Plant, Nurture, Flourish, Serve 'It's like a mustard seed that man took and planted in his garden. It grew and became a tree and the birds in the sky nested in its branches'. Luke 13:19
Our vision encapsulates everything we do, from the way we conduct ourselves, both children and adults, to the way we try to do our best every day in school, whether trying our best in Maths, or trying to regulate our behaviour.
Our vision underpins our school rules:
Our vision is displayed throughout the school to remind children, staff and the community that our vision drives our actions, thoughts and behaviours.
As part of our Inset Day on 1st September 2026, as a staff we considered what our vision meant to us. Please see the images below to see what all staff members thought.
From our staff thoughts, a word art was created:
Woven into our vision, are our twelve school values that guide us in the ways that we seek to do things at Box Church of England School. These are based on the Christian faith, but are values that are important to us, whatever our faith or background.
We talk and learn about these values through collective worship and in class, but we try to put them into practice in every situation at school. At Box we live our values.
We have twelve values which we have chosen for our school. We learn about these in school, thinking about one value in detail each term:
Through our collective worship work, we reflect on key questions each week, before spending time in class reflection on our Big Question.
Plant, Nurture, Flourish, Serve
'It's like a mustard seed that man took and planted in his garden. It grew and became a tree and the birds in the sky nested in its branches'. Luke 13:19
At the end of the term, we record all our Values work in our Values' Shield Impact Book. Children who have been noted by school staff are awarded the Values shield to recognise going 'above and beyond' in their display of the Value.
2026–2027 Values: Big Questions reflection
Term 1 Friendship A friend loves at all times – Proverbs 7:17
Term 2 Perseverance I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me – Philippians 4:13
Term 3 Peace In me you may have peace – John 16
Term 4 Truthfulness The truth will set you free – John 8:32
Term 5 Compassion Be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving each other, just as in Christ God forgave you – Ephesians 4
Term 6 Creativity Yes, you can – Philippians
2027–2028 Values: Big Questions reflection
Term 1 Responsibility Matthew 24 14–30 You are responsible for the talent that has been entrusted to you.
Term 2 Trust Ecclesiastes 4.9-10 Two people are better than one … If one person falls, the other can reach out to help.
Term 3 Courage Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged by the Lord, your God will be with you wherever you go. Joshua 19
Term 4 Forgiveness Just as the Lord has forgiven you, so you must forgive others Colossians 3:13
Term 5 Wisdom is better than strength Proverbs 13:20 He who walks with the wise grows wise Ecclesiastes 9:16
Term 6 Sharing God loves a cheerful giver 2 Corinthians 9:7
Our oldest children in school, Sycamore class, have already started to consider what our values mean to them and have created a lovely display in school.
Thank you Sycamore class for your lovely thoughts.
From our vision and values is our ethos of Be your best! All we want from our children is that they use our vision and values to just try their best. This is our very first rule in Box:
Plant the seeds of learning, by trying your best every day.
Our weekly certificates are also based on this. Each week two children are selected to receive a certificate from their class teacher.
Vision and the school garden.
We are very fortunate at Box to have a beautiful school garden, that our vision relates to. Our school garden is a very special and unique part of our school and is enjoyed for its beauty as well as a place to play and learn. On their journey through school, children are taught gardening jobs and are responsible for areas of the garden. There are many opportunities for them to plant seeds, nurture plants and watch them flourish. During our work on the vision, the children are helped to explore how 'plant, nurture, flourish, serve' is a metaphor that can be applied to many aspects of their life.
We plant a wide range of seeds in our children in the form of knowledge, skills and new experiences; we nurture their development (providing extra support where needed) to enable all children to flourish. Children are given opportunities to serve by supporting and helping others, sharing work and expertise and by having responsibilities such as looking after a reception buddy, being a young leader or serving on a school committee such as eco-schools.

PE and Sports Premium
Vision for the Primary PE and Sport Premium: PE and Sport is very important to us at Box.
Intent: Physical Education at Box.
In order for all children to achieve their full potential and to aim for our school vision of 'Plant, Nurture, Flourish, Serve,' we have developed a PE scheme of work which enables children to develop their core Physical Education skills, and enables them to participate in structured competitive activities at differing levels:
A high-quality physical education curriculum inspires all pupils to succeed and excel in competitive sport and other physically-demanding activities. It should provide opportunities for pupils to become physically confident in a way which supports their health and fitness. Opportunities to compete in sport and other activities build character and help to embed some of our school values such as: friendship, perseverance, truthfulness, and respect.
Quality First Wave Teaching: Intent of the PE curriculum
All children receive a broad and balanced PE curriculum as part of QFWT (Quality First wave Teaching). This is about what should be on offer for all children: the effective inclusion of all pupils in high-quality everyday personalised teaching. Such teaching will, for example, be based on clear objectives that are shared with the children and returned to at the end of the lesson; carefully explained new PE vocabulary; use of lively, interactive teaching styles and also make maximum use of visual and kinaesthetic as well as auditory/verbal learning. The objectives that are used are taken from the school’s skills and progression grid, which is taken explicitly from the National Curriculum for PE.
Implementation: The objectives that are implemented across the school's scheme of work are taken from the school’s skills and progression grid (see example in attachment below) which is taken explicitly from the National Curriculum for PE.
These skills are mapped out each term to enable children to develop their own aptitude in Physical Education.
Across the year, the children experience a broad range of curriculum activities away from more traditional games. The rationale behind this move to less traditional PE subjects is based on the context of the school and the reasoning that the vast majority of our children access local sporting clubs. Therefore, we have decided to develop a Games' curriculum that is innovate in developing activities in sports such as Handball, Dodgeball, Tennis, Basketball. OOA and Swimming objectives are covered discretely.
One class will have a block of swimming lessons. We use our swimming provision to endeavour to see that ‘all children by the time they leave primary school are able to swim 25 metres.’ Children are assessed at the end of Year6 on whether they can swim 25 metres. If they cannot, this is highlighted early to secondary school.
OOA activities are covered by Year 6 Camp and through other enrichment activities throughout the year. All children in Year 6 have access to these OOA activities.
Intra – school competition: As part of developing the school's values further and in order to enable children to develop opportunities to compete in competitive sport and other activities that build character, all children are given the opportunity to take part in intra-school competitions. These competitions can range from school sports day to cricket tournaments that are arranged to find a winning house team.
Inter – school competition: In order to enable children to develop opportunities to compete in competitive sport and other activities that build character, some children are given the opportunity to take part in Inter-school competitions. These competitions enables us to challenge those children who need the additional experience of competing against other schools. These experiences are invaluable to children to build their character, and to instil the school values of respect and friendship, as the children will experience the winning and losing feeling and know how to react in both situations.
Impact: A high-quality physical education curriculum and extra-curriculum inspires all pupils to succeed and excel in competitive sport and other physically-demanding activities. It should provide opportunities for pupils to become physically confident in a way which supports their health and fitness. Opportunities to compete in sport and other activities build character and help to embed some of our school values, such as: friendship, perseverance, truthfulness, and respect.
Alongside PE lessons, school are given a small budget to use to help develop PE and Physical activity in school. In line with the DFE's new online reporting system, please see below the links to the confirmation of our school's funding allocation, the way it was spent and more importantly the impact and sustainability of PE and Sport at Box.
Please note in May 2026, schools were told that the PE funding will cease. We are awaiting details of the funding for the academic year 2026-2027.
2025-26 Funding Impact:
With the additional PE Premium funding we receive, we have sought to use it to inspire our children to be 'flourishing' in the subject and to develop further experiences that they might not have the opportunity to do so. Our vision also lends itself to developing our children’s physical health and well-being and is a key aim of the use of PE primary funding.

Reading
Reading at Our School
Reading is prioritised across our Trust and our school as we recognise the importance this plays in securing the life chances of all our children.
Our vision of Plant, Nurture, Flourish, Serve is reflected strongly in our approach to reading. We believe that learning to read is one of the most important foundations we can plant for every child. Through high-quality teaching, rich language experiences, carefully chosen texts and a love of reading, we nurture children's knowledge, vocabulary, confidence and curiosity so that they can flourish as readers, learners and individuals.
Reading opens doors. It enables children to access the full curriculum, develop their understanding of the world and communicate their ideas effectively. It also provides opportunities to experience different lives, cultures, perspectives and possibilities. In this way, reading helps children to understand themselves and others and prepares them to make a positive contribution to their communities and the wider world.
If our children cannot read well, they cannot access the full curriculum, which means they will struggle to learn.
We want all children to read fluently by the end of primary school so that they are confident and well equipped to flourish in their next stage of education and beyond.
We recognise that learning to read is an incredibly complex process for children and there are many strands of the English Language structure that have to be understood and mastered.
Our role is to plant strong foundations, nurture developing readers and provide the knowledge, skills and confidence children need to flourish.
Understanding How Children Learn to Read
Reading well involves two main parts that work together:
1. Understanding What You Read (Language Comprehension)
This is about making sense of the words and ideas:
Knowing about the world (background knowledge).
Knowing word meanings (vocabulary).
Understanding grammar and sentence structure (which words to use in the correct order together with the right punctuation).
Thinking about what the text means by reading between the lines (working something out from clues in the text).
Knowing how stories and texts work (this usually develops from being frequently read to by an adult).
Developing language comprehension is an important part of nurturing readers. Through rich conversation, stories and exposure to a wide range of texts, we help children develop the knowledge and language they need to understand what they read and engage with the world around them.
2. Reading the Words (Word Recognition)
This is about the mechanics:
Hearing and recognising the sounds that letters and combinations of letters make (phonological awareness).
Putting the sounds together to read words (decoding).
Recognising words quickly that often don't make sense when the sounds are put together (sight recognition).
By explicitly teaching these skills, we plant the foundations for successful reading and enable children to develop the automaticity they need to become increasingly fluent and independent readers.
How Do We Teach Children to Read?
To develop rich knowledge and skills, children are explicitly taught daily word reading. Alongside this, children are exposed to language comprehension through our 'Talk Through Stories' approach. Word reading development is embedded into our phonics programme.
Once children become more phonologically aware, the focus of reading shifts towards developing fluent reading.
We recognise that every child develops as a reader at their own pace. Through high-quality teaching, careful assessment and appropriate support, we seek to identify and remove barriers so that every child can develop confidence and experience success.
Our aim is to nurture children as readers, building not only their technical ability but also their confidence, curiosity and enjoyment.
What is Talk Through Stories?
Talk Through Stories is an approach designed to help young children develop language, comprehension and vocabulary through structured story time sessions.
This approach builds a strong foundation in language and literacy and supports children to develop crucial speaking and listening skills.
Key elements of this approach:
1. Story-Based Learning
Children engage deeply with a high-quality picture book over the course of a week or more.
2. Repetition and Discussion
The same story is read multiple times, with daily discussions to build understanding and confidence.
3. Vocabulary Development
Key words from the story are explicitly taught and reinforced through conversation and play.
4. Oral Language Skills
The focus is on talking - children are encouraged to describe, explain and retell parts of the story using new vocabulary.
5. Comprehension Focus
Teachers guide children through the story structure, character motivations and key themes.
Talk Through Stories helps us nurture children's language and imagination, providing rich experiences that support them to become confident communicators and thoughtful readers.
How Do We Teach Phonics?
At Box we use Unlocking Letters and Sounds.
In Year 1, once children have learnt a number of sounds and can put these together to read words, they need daily practice in reading.
We use an approach called 'scaffolded reading'. The teacher shows the children how to read at the right speed, use expression and stop at the right places. They also model how to sound out words and put the sounds together.
Children then read the text back to the teacher – this is called repeated reading. As the year progresses, children then begin to practise reading the text to partners while the teacher moves around the room 'listening in'.
This carefully structured approach helps children move from developing the mechanics of reading towards becoming fluent, confident and increasingly independent readers.
Once children have completed the phonics programme (usually during Year 2), they experience different types of reading lessons, each aimed at developing fluent, confident readers:
Fluency means being able to read smoothly and understand what you are reading. A fluent reader can read words correctly, quickly and easily, and with expression.
Accuracy: Reading words correctly without mistakes.
Automaticity: Reading quickly and easily. How fast a child reads depends on their reading skill, purpose, and whether they read out loud or silently.
Prosody: Reading with the right tone, rhythm and expression – like natural speech.
Teaching children to read fluently is essential because fluency serves as the bridge between decoding (sounding out words) and understanding them.
When readers don't have to focus on decoding each word, they can better understand the text's meaning, make connections to what they already know and build a mental picture of the text.
Developing fluency enables children to move beyond the mechanics of reading and flourish as confident readers. It gives them greater access to the curriculum and allows them to engage more deeply with ideas, information and stories.
What Do We Mean by Extended Read?
An Extended Read is a structure for teaching reading that is designed to give children plenty of experience of the written English Language.
An Extended Read allows children to spend more time focusing on a longer text to improve reading fluency, vocabulary and an understanding of the structure of the text.
The aim is to help children build reading stamina and understand the main ideas of the text.
Extended reading provides opportunities for children to flourish through sustained engagement with increasingly complex texts, developing the knowledge, vocabulary and reading stamina they will need throughout their education and beyond.
What Do We Mean by Close Reading?
Close Reading is a structure for teaching reading that is designed to engage children in deeper exploration of texts. A shorter piece of the current text is used to zoom into and discuss.
The aim of Close Reading is to carefully consider the ways authors use language and the impact that this language has on different readers.
Through the discussion of texts, children are encouraged to see that texts can be understood in different ways and that these views and opinions can be discussed.
Close Reading helps children to become thoughtful and critical readers. It encourages them to question, discuss, interpret and respond to what they read, helping them to develop the confidence to express their own ideas while respecting the perspectives of others.
These are important qualities not only for academic success, but for children as they grow into confident individuals who can serve and contribute positively to their communities and the wider world.
How Do We Support Children to Develop Reading for Pleasure?
Reading is about more than learning a skill. We want children to develop a lifelong love of reading.
We want every child to experience the joy, wonder, curiosity and escape that books can provide. Through reading for pleasure, children can explore different worlds, encounter new ideas, develop empathy and discover authors, characters and subjects that inspire them.
We aim to create a culture where reading is valued, celebrated and shared across our school community. Children are given opportunities to hear high-quality texts read aloud, recommend books to one another, talk about what they have read and choose books that reflect their interests and introduce them to new experiences.
We recognise that reading for pleasure can nurture children's imagination, vocabulary, knowledge and wellbeing. It can also help children develop a stronger understanding of themselves and others.
Our vision of Plant, Nurture, Flourish, Serve is therefore central to our approach to reading:
Plant – we plant strong foundations through systematic phonics, language development, vocabulary and high-quality teaching.
Nurture – we nurture children's confidence, curiosity and enjoyment through rich stories, conversation, carefully chosen texts and supportive teaching.
Flourish – we enable children to become fluent, confident and enthusiastic readers who can access the full curriculum and continue to grow as learners.
Serve – we develop readers who can understand different perspectives, communicate effectively, engage thoughtfully with the world and use their knowledge and understanding to contribute positively to others.
We want every child to leave our primary school knowing that reading can open doors – to knowledge, imagination, opportunity and possibility.
Most importantly, we want our children to leave us as confident, capable and enthusiastic readers who are ready to flourish in the next stage of their education and throughout their lives.

pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Our Curriculum Intent
At Box Church of England Primary School, our curriculum is rooted in our Christian vision: Plant, Nurture, Flourish, Serve. We want every child to be known, valued and encouraged to flourish as a unique individual, equipped with the knowledge, skills, values and confidence to make a positive difference in the world around them.
Our curriculum is ambitious, purposeful and rooted in our community. It builds on the strengths of our children, our school and our village, whilst opening windows to the wider world. Through rich and meaningful learning experiences, we encourage children to ask questions, think deeply, explore different perspectives and develop a growing understanding of their place within God’s world.
Plant
We plant the foundations for lifelong learning. Children develop a strong knowledge base alongside the essential skills of reading, writing, mathematics, science, computing and communication. We nurture curiosity, creativity and a love of learning, providing children with the secure foundations they need to thrive.
Nurture
We nurture the whole child. Our Christian values of respect, compassion, courage, forgiveness and justice are woven through school life and our curriculum. We create opportunities for children to develop resilience, confidence, collaboration and empathy, learning how to listen to others, appreciate difference and respond thoughtfully to the challenges they encounter.
Flourish
We want every child to flourish. Our curriculum is broad, balanced and connected, enabling children to make meaningful links between subjects and apply their learning in different contexts. Through our curriculum, children explore the relationships between people, places, subjects, the past, the present and the future. We deliberately provide opportunities for children to think critically and creatively, solve problems, communicate effectively and become increasingly independent learners. The
Serve
We encourage our children to serve others and to recognise that they have the power to make a difference. Our curriculum connects children with their local community, the wider world and the challenges facing society and our planet. Through real-life experiences and opportunities to explore citizenship and global issues, children learn that their voices matter and that they can act with courage, compassion and hope.
Our curriculum therefore reaches beyond the classroom. Children learn about their local heritage and community while developing an understanding of their responsibilities as global citizens. They consider the impact of the choices they make today on future generations and are encouraged to become courageous advocates.
At the heart of our curriculum is the belief that learning should be meaningful, memorable and connected. We make purposeful links across subjects where this deepens understanding, while ensuring that subjects such as Science, RE, and PE retain their own identity and disciplinary knowledge. By focusing on depth rather than simply covering content, we give children time to secure knowledge, practise skills and develop genuine understanding.
Ultimately, our curriculum seeks to prepare children not simply for the next stage of their education, but for life. We want them to leave Box as confident, compassionate and courageous young people who know that they belong, understand their responsibility to others and feel empowered to use their gifts to make a positive difference.
We plant the foundations, nurture potential, help every child flourish and inspire them to serve others.
Plant. Nurture. Flourish. Serve.
As a mixed-age school, we have carefully designed our curriculum around a two-year cycle, ensuring that learning is both progressive and accessible to all children within a class. The cycle provides a clear sequence of learning, with knowledge and skills carefully built upon and revisited over time. This approach allows teachers to respond to the different ages, starting points and needs of our pupils, while ensuring that no child misses out on essential learning. Careful consideration has been given to the order in which knowledge and skills are taught, so that each year builds meaningfully on what has come before and prepares children for what comes next.

History
The school was originally set up in the church and when it out grew the church it moved into the workhouse next door. The workhouse eventually fell into disrepair and the present Victorian building was built in 1875 with capacity for 400 children in three separate sections for boys, girls and infants.
The history of the school is well documented and all original documents are stored in the Swindon and Wiltshire History Centre in Chippenham and can be viewed by visitors to the centre. Over the years these documents have been studied in detail, particularly by Canon John Ayers who has a long association with the school and has summarised the history of the school in a document called ‘A Christian and Useful Education’. On this page you will also find links to other documents such as well as extracts from our school log books.
In 2008 we celebrated our 300th anniversary and as part of our celebrations relived aspects of the school’s history, such as the workhouse lunch, with past and present pupils, parents and members of the local community.
To learn more of history of Box School and the studies of Canon John Ayers, please read his writings, Box Charity School.
At the start of April 2024, the school became an academy and we joined the Mosaic Partnership Trust.

Inclusion: Special Educational Needs & Disability
Box CE and The Mosaic Partnership Trust – Our Inclusion Vision:At Box, we believe that every child has a unique and evolving profile of strengths, interests and needs. We are committed to creating an inclusive school community where every child feels valued, understood and supported to achieve their potential.
Our vision of Plant, Nurture, Flourish, Serve underpins our approach to inclusion. We believe that every child should have the opportunity to plant strong foundations, be nurtured through positive relationships and responsive support, flourish as a learner and individual, and develop the confidence, character and independence to contribute positively to others and their community.
Through an ambitious curriculum, inclusive teaching, enabling learning environments, adaptive practice and meaningful partnerships with families, we work to remove barriers and create a culture where every child can access learning, participate fully in school life, develop increasing independence and experience a genuine sense of belonging.
Inclusion is not a bolt-on. It is at the heart of everything we do. It is woven throughout our curriculum, classrooms, relationships and everyday practice, shaping the way we teach, support and celebrate every learner.
Through high-quality teaching, enabling learning environments, adaptive practice and meaningful partnerships with families, we aim to ensure that every child can participate, belong, flourish and develop their capacity to serve others.
Our Inclusive Curriculum
We believe that inclusion begins with an ambitious curriculum and high-quality teaching for all.
Our curriculum is designed to:
Promote participation, achievement and belonging.
Develop knowledge, skills and understanding over time.
Celebrate diversity and value difference.
Build confidence, resilience and independence.
Provide appropriate challenge and opportunities for success.
Prepare children for future learning and life beyond school.
Through our curriculum, we seek to plant strong foundations for learning and personal development, nurturing children's curiosity and confidence and providing the knowledge and experiences they need to flourish.
We recognise that children may access learning in different ways and that some may require adaptations and additional support to achieve success. Our commitment is to maintain high expectations while ensuring that barriers are identified and addressed.
Universal Inclusive Teaching
High-quality teaching is the foundation of our inclusive approach. At Mosaic, inclusion is not something additional to teaching. It is how teaching is designed. Universal Inclusive Teaching provides the foundation for all learners and helps remove barriers before they arise.
Across our classrooms you will see:
Clear explanations and modelling.
Carefully sequenced learning.
Explicit teaching of vocabulary and concepts.
Regular opportunities for practice and retrieval.
Positive relationships and high expectations.
Flexible approaches that support different ways of learning.
Scaffolds that help children experience success whilst developing independence.
This approach helps us plant secure foundations for every learner, while ensuring that children are appropriately supported and challenged to grow in confidence, develop independence and flourish.
Enabling Learning Environments
We know that children's ability to learn, participate and succeed is influenced not only by what is taught but by the environment in which they learn.
Our environments are designed to promote accessibility, participation, wellbeing, independence and belonging for all learners.
We recognise that children are more likely to thrive when they feel safe, understood, represented and connected to their school community. Through clear routines, positive relationships, communication-friendly approaches and thoughtfully organised learning spaces, we create the conditions in which all children can participate, engage and flourish.
We seek to nurture a sense of safety, belonging and confidence, helping children to become increasingly secure and independent in their learning and relationships.
Our Mosaic Adaptive Practice Framework helps staff understand and respond to barriers that children may experience.
Adaptations are not about lowering expectations; they are about removing barriers so that every child can access learning, participate fully and experience success. Staff use a combination of planned and responsive adaptations to ensure teaching remains flexible and inclusive.
Our adaptive approach reflects our belief that children do not all need the same thing to succeed. By understanding each child and responding thoughtfully to their needs, we can nurture their strengths, remove barriers and create the conditions in which they can flourish.
Planned adaptations are identified in advance through assessment, observation, pupil voice, family partnerships and professional knowledge of the child.
They are thoughtfully incorporated into teaching, learning environments and routines to reduce barriers before they arise.
Responsive Adaptations
Responsive adaptations are made in the moment as staff respond to children's understanding, participation, confidence and wellbeing.
This responsive approach enables staff to recognise when a child needs additional support, a different approach or greater challenge, ensuring that teaching remains responsive to the learner in front of us.
The Importance of Independence
A key principle of our approach is helping children become increasingly independent.
The purpose of adaptations is not to create dependence on adult support. Instead, we aim to equip children with the knowledge, skills, strategies and confidence they need to access learning, solve problems, communicate effectively and participate successfully in school life.
Through carefully planned support, we help children develop the independence they need to thrive both now and in the future.
This is an important part of our Flourish and Serve vision. As children grow in confidence and independence, we want them to recognise their own strengths, understand their responsibilities and develop the skills and character to make a positive contribution to the lives of others.
Partnership with Families
We believe that meaningful inclusion is built through strong relationships, shared understanding and genuine partnership.
Children thrive when the adults around them work together to understand their strengths, aspirations and experiences, creating a consistent and supportive approach across home and school.
We value the knowledge, perspectives and lived experiences of children and their families and recognise the important role they play in shaping inclusive practice.
Through open communication, collaboration and shared decision-making, we aim to ensure that children and families feel heard, respected and actively involved in decisions about support, provision and school life.
We work alongside families to:
Understand children's strengths, interests, aspirations and support needs.
Share successes, achievements and progress.
Identify and reduce barriers to learning, participation and wellbeing.
Review support and evaluate its impact together.
Listen to and act upon the views of children and their families.
Co-produce approaches that help children thrive both in school and beyond.
Strong family partnerships help us to nurture children consistently, celebrate their progress and create the shared conditions in which they can flourish.
Participation, Belonging and Thriving
Ensuring every child can engage meaningfully in learning, relationships and the wider life of the school.
We want every child to have access to the opportunities, experiences and relationships that enable them to develop their strengths, discover their interests and contribute to school life.
Creating an inclusive culture where every child and family feels welcomed, valued, understood and connected.
We believe belonging is fundamental to learning, wellbeing and participation. It is developed through positive relationships, strengths-based practice, inclusive environments, meaningful family partnerships and a culture that celebrates diversity and values difference.
When children feel that they belong, they are better placed to flourish as confident and engaged learners.
Supporting every child to achieve, grow in confidence, develop independence and flourish as a learner and individual.
For us, thriving means more than academic success. It means developing the knowledge, skills, confidence, character and relationships needed to navigate life successfully and make a positive contribution to others.
This reflects our wider vision of Plant, Nurture, Flourish, Serve:
Plant – establishing strong foundations for learning, belonging, confidence and aspiration.
Nurture – developing children through positive relationships, responsive support and high expectations.
Flourish – enabling every child to achieve, grow in confidence, develop independence and fulfil their potential.
Serve – helping children recognise their strengths, value others and develop the character and confidence to contribute positively to their community and the wider world.

If you have any concerns you would like to talk to us about, please make an appointment with your child’s class teacher. Together, you can make a decision about how to tackle the issue and what the next steps are. It may be that the concern can be resolved between you and the class teacher, or alternatively, it might warrant the intervention of our school’s Inclusion Manager/SENCo, Cathy Clack. The Inclusion Manager will aim to offer help and advice in a variety of ways through our special educational needs and disability provision (SEND) and in some cases through the advice and support of external agencies.
Please contact Cathy if you would like to have a chat about any inclusion issues such as Special Educational Needs via the school office or email catherine.clack@box.wilts.sch.uk
Similarly, if you feel that any outside factors (perhaps a family issue, i.e. separation or bereavement or even a medical issue) may have an impact on your child's learning and well-being, it is vitally important that you keep the school informed.
